# Panel of the batch runner (batch.py): one cartridge of the roms directory
# per line, with the number of frames to run and the pad script, in the
# SIMPAD format: "frame:bits,..." gives the buttons held from each frame on,
# bits in hexadecimal (01 up, 02 down, 04 left, 08 right, 10 button 1,
# 20 button 2, 100 pause). "-" keeps the default (frames: the -frames
# option; pad: button 1 tapped every 300 frames). Cartridges absent from
# this file run with the defaults.
#
# A run on the console or on Phoenix writes its own entry at the pause or
# the end of the run (the "Pad script:" line of the log, which the ISO's
# pad recorder builds from the frames where the buttons changed); such a
# replay may diverge in a timing-sensitive game, since translated and
# interpreted code take interrupts at different boundaries.
#
# The scripts aim at reaching the game itself, then at simple inputs that
# keep it busy (walking, jumping, firing), since the model's timings are
# only meaningful in play. The cartridges are chosen by the hardware
# mechanisms they use: line interrupts and raster effects (Road Rash,
# OutRun, Space Harrier), many sprites and the per-line limit (R-Type,
# Power Strike, Sonic Chaos), big sprites streamed to VRAM (Golden Axe,
# Shinobi), cartridge RAM (Phantasy Star, Ys), a non-Sega mapper and the
# 224-line display mode (Micro Machines), colour RAM writes during the
# active display (Space Harrier), RAM code (Ys), VRAM reads and counters
# (Zillion, Golvellius).
#
# cartridge          frames  pad script
